extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news consumers, trustees, corporate stakeholders, and employees of Thomson Reuters
extracted.subtask_description: A corporate statement of binding principles and governance mechanisms that define how a major news organisation (Thomson Reuters/Reuters) must preserve independence, integrity, and freedom from bias in gathering and distributing news and information.

rubrics_metrics.name: That Reuters shall at no time pass into the hands of any one interest, group, or faction
rubrics_metrics.description: That Reuters shall at no time pass into the hands of any one interest, group, or faction;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust Principles require institutional safeguards to prevent control by a single interest. A Founders Share structure and contractual arrangements were created to achieve this when Reuters became a public company. The Thomson Reuters Founders Share Company holds special rights to block or limit transfers of control over the Reuters news business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve integrity, independence, and freedom from bias at all times
rubrics_metrics.description: That the integrity, independence, and freedom from bias of Thomson Reuters shall at all times be fully preserved;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thomson Reuters is obliged and committed to apply the Trust Principles to its operations. The company’s charter documents include provisions to safeguard these principles and require directors to have due regard to them when performing their duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply unbiased and reliable news services
rubrics_metrics.description: That Reuters shall supply unbiased and reliable news services to newspapers, news agencies, broadcasters, and other media subscribers and to businesses, governments, institutions, individuals, and others with whom Reuters has or may have contracts;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle governs gathering and dissemination of information and news: services must be reliable and objective for a wide range of clients and contractual partners. The page emphasises customers depend on reliable and objective news and information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay due regard to the many interests served beyond the media
rubrics_metrics.description: That Thomson Reuters shall pay due regard to the many interests which it serves in addition to those of the media;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuters should consider multiple stakeholder interests (e.g., businesses, governments, institutions, the public) when exercising its editorial and business decisions, not only the interests of media customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continual expansion, development, and adaptation of news and services
rubrics_metrics.description: That no effort shall be spared to expand, develop, and adapt the news and other services and products of Thomson Reuters so as to maintain its leading position in the international news and information business
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organisation should actively pursue improvements and innovation in its news and information products to retain leadership internationally; this is presented as an obligation alongside editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational and governance obligation to apply the Trust Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Thomson Reuters itself is obliged and committed to apply the Trust Principles to its operations. The charter documents of Thomson Reuters Corporation include provisions to safeguard the Trust Principles as they apply to the Thomson Reuters business and require Thomson Reuters Directors, in the performance of their duties, to have due regard to the Trust Principles, by the proper exercise of their powers and in accordance with their other duties as Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust Principles are embedded into corporate charter and director duties to ensure operational application; directors are legally required to consider these principles when making decisions affecting the news business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founders Share Company special rights to protect the Trust Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Founders Share and other contractual arrangements now confer a number of special rights upon the Thomson Reuters Founders Share Company. For example, (i) the Thomson Reuters Founders Share Company has enhanced voting rights in circumstances where someone is seeking to obtain a significant shareholding in, or acquire control of, Thomson Reuters and (ii) the prior consent of the Thomson Reuters Founders Share Company must be sought prior to undertaking any sale of, or other material transaction involving, the Reuters news business unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legal/structural mechanism (Founders Share Company) was created to enable enforcement of the Trust Principles in ownership and transaction decisions; it can block or condition changes that might threaten editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustees' role, composition, selection, meetings, and duties to ensure compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The directors of Thomson Reuters Founders Share Company (known as ‘Trustees’) have a duty to ensure, to the extent possible, that the Trust Principles are complied with. The Trustees are experienced and eminent people from diverse arenas in politics, diplomacy, media, public service and business. The Trustees are selected by a nomination committee and proposed to the board of the Thomson Reuters Founders Share Company for appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection/nomination committee details: the nomination committee assists in scrutinising candidates’ suitability and its members include two persons appointed by the chairman after consultation with the European Court of Human Rights and representatives of certain press associations. The Thomson Reuters Corporation board has two representatives on the nomination committee. The Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Founders Share Company Board are members of the nomination committee; the Chairman appoints three other directors as members and acts as chairman of the committee. Operational requirements: number of Trustees must be at least 14 and not more than 18; Trustees have a minimum of two meetings per year; they receive reports on activities across the business and meet with the Thomson Reuters Board and senior management to maintain regular contact and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard independence to maintain customer trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Customers across the world depend on us to provide them with reliable and objective news and information. This means that we have a special need to safeguard our independence and integrity and avoid any bias which may stem from control by specific individuals or interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence and objectivity are explicitly tied to commercial reputation and customer reliance; the Trust Principles are presented as fundamental to the entire business and its relationship with customers.
